relationship.statement: A simple pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, growing with the square root of length while bob mass has no effect. For small release angles, changing how far back you pull it changes speed and width without changing the timing.
assumptions: Air resistance and pivot friction are neglected so total mechanical energy stays constant.
The rod or string is massless and rigid, with all bob mass concentrated at a point.
Gravity is fixed at 9.81 m/s^2 and the small-angle approximation is used.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the fixed pivot point to the center of the bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the suspended bob, varied to test whether weight alters timing.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle pulled away from the vertical equilibrium line.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration held constant at Earth surface value.

quantities.label: Swing period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of full back-and-forth swings completed each second.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point.

quantities.label: Current angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angular position measured from straight down.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var L = inputs.L; var m = inputs.m; var theta0 = inputs.theta0; var theta0Rad = theta0 * Math.PI / 180; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var T = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var f = 1 / T; var v_max = Math.sqrt(g * L) * theta0Rad; var phase = omega * t; var thetaRad = theta0Rad * Math.cos(phase); var theta = theta0 * Math.cos(phase); var dthetaDt = -theta0Rad * omega * Math.sin(phase); var bob_x = -1.0 + L * Math.sin(thetaRad); var bob_y = -L * Math.cos(thetaRad); var vx = L * Math.cos(thetaRad) * dthetaDt; var vy = L * Math.sin(thetaRad) * dthetaDt; var vel_x = bob_x + 0.35 * vx; var vel_y = bob_y + 0.35 * vy; var eq_y = -L; var bob_size = 0.25 + 0.65 * (m - 0.5) / 4.5; var L_ref = 1.0; var theta0_ref = 20; var theta0RefRad = theta0_ref * Math.PI / 180; var omegaRef = Math.sqrt(g / L_ref); var refPhase = omegaRef * t; var refThetaRad = theta0RefRad * Math.cos(refPhase); var ref_theta = theta0_ref * Math.cos(refPhase); var ref_x = 1.1 + L_ref * Math.sin(refThetaRad); var ref_y = -L_ref * Math.cos(refThetaRad); var is_slower = L > 1.05; var is_faster = L < 0.95; return { T: T, f: f, v_max: v_max, theta: theta, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, vel_x: vel_x, vel_y: vel_y, eq_y: eq_y, bob_size: bob_size, ref_theta: ref_theta, ref_x: ref_x, ref_y: ref_y, is_slower: is_slower, is_faster: is_faster }; }

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum against a 1 m reference as you vary length, bob mass, and release angle. Watch both pendulums swing and track their angles over time.
lesson.instructions: Adjust string length, bob mass, and release angle with the sliders, then watch the swing and the angle-time graph beside the 1 m reference.
lesson.goal: Only string length changes a pendulum's period under small swings; bob mass has no effect, and wider release raises speed without changing timing.
